What we work on

Phonics and early reading (ages 4–6)

Letter sounds, blending and segmenting, reading fluency and first sentences. A secure start in phonics makes every later stage of English easier, so I take the time to get it right.

KS1 and KS2 English (ages 5–11)

Reading comprehension, vocabulary, spelling, grammar and punctuation, plus creative and non-fiction writing. Lessons follow what your child is learning at school and fill any gaps along the way.

KS2 SATs English

Preparation for the Year 6 reading paper and the grammar, punctuation and spelling tests: the question types, how to manage the time, and how to check answers.

11+ and school entrance English

Comprehension, inference, vocabulary and creative writing for 7+, 8+ and 11+ papers at grammar and independent schools. More about 11+ preparation.

GCSE English Language and Literature

Analysing unseen extracts, revising set texts, planning and structuring essays, and timed writing practice, with a clear focus on what the mark scheme rewards. More about GCSE tuition.

How lessons work

We start with a short phone call about your child, their school and what you'd like to improve. Every lesson after that is planned around your child: what they're covering at school, where they're getting stuck, and what they need next. I'm a PGCE-qualified teacher with Qualified Teacher Status, over 10 years' UK classroom experience and an Enhanced DBS check.

body:
What I prepare children for

  • 11+ for grammar and independent schools, in Maths and English
  • 7+ and 8+ independent school entrance, in Maths and English
  • 4+ early-years assessments: early reading, number and confidence

What we cover

11+ English

Reading comprehension and inference, vocabulary, spelling, grammar and punctuation, and creative writing to a time limit.

11+ Maths

Arithmetic, multi-step problem solving and reasoning, including topics that go beyond the Year 5 school curriculum, practised for speed as well as accuracy.

Exam technique

Timed practice papers, pacing, checking answers and staying calm on the day. Children who know the format do better than those meeting it for the first time.

I teach the Maths and English papers. If the schools you're applying to also test verbal or non-verbal reasoning, tell me when we first speak and we'll talk about how to cover it.

When to start

Most grammar school 11+ exams are sat in September of Year 6, so many families start preparing in Year 4 or Year 5. Starting earlier means steady weekly lessons rather than a rush at the end. If your child's exam is sooner, call me and we'll work out a realistic plan.

Why parents choose me

I'm a PGCE-qualified teacher with Qualified Teacher Status, over 10 years' UK classroom experience and an Enhanced DBS check. Every 11+ plan is built for your child, not taken from a template.
